entities.summary:
Francisco de Borja y Navarro de Alpicat (1450-1511) was a Spanish cardinal and the seventh of ten cardinal-nephews created by Pope Alexander VI, whose nepotism scandal would forever tarnish the Church's reputation.

 Born into a wealthy and influential family, Francisco de Borja was appointed cardinal at the age of 18, becoming the youngest cardinal in history. His rapid rise to power and wealth was facilitated by his family's connections and the Church's corrupt practices.

 Francis de Borja's tenure as cardinal was marked by several significant events, including the Concorso di San Pietro, a papal conclave that led to the election of Pope Julius II, and his involvement in the politics of the Italian city-states.

 Francis de Borja's legacy is that of a symbol of the Church's corruption and the dangers of nepotism, as well as a reminder of the immense power and influence wielded by the Catholic Church during the Renaissance. His story serves as a cautionary tale about the risks of unchecked power and the corrupting influence of wealth and privilege.

 The sheer audacity of his rise to power, the scandal that surrounded his appointment, and the lasting impact on the Church's reputation make Francisco de Borja a fascinating figure in the annals of history, a testament to the complexities and contradictions of the Renaissance era.
